title: Rust-Hybrid Indexing Completion And Performance Roadmap
description: Rebuild the roadmap around Rust-owned indexing/finalization ownership migration, with performance as evidence and guardrail.

1.label: Rust-Hybrid Indexing Completion And Performance Roadmap

decisions.answer: Complete Rust-owned indexing/finalization roadmap reconstruction and make performance optimization serve that ownership migration mainline.
decisions.note: Chosen over continuing a narrow performance-candidate queue.

decisions.answer: Use ownership migration as the trunk; use end-to-end indexing path inside each ownership area; use user outcome as guardrails.
decisions.note: This avoids letting performance grow into a separate maze.

1-1.label: Current fact base and evidence archive
1-1.notes: Completed by consolidating facts from the previous performance roadmaps and benchmark closeouts.

1-2.label: Rust-owned indexing completion boundary

decisions.answer: For JS, JSX, TS, TSX, MTS, CTS, and Go, indexing plus resolver plus finalization should become as Rust-owned as practical.
decisions.note: TypeScript remains product shell, fallback orchestration, non-Rust-owned language support, and explicitly unmigrated semantic guardrails.

1-2.notes: Boundary direction recorded: supported JS/TS variants and Go should become as Rust-owned as practical; TS remains product shell and fallback/guardrail owner.

decisions.answer: Prioritize resolver/finalization ownership frontier.
decisions.note: VS Code sparse evidence points to finalization/reference-resolution tail after Rust core extraction/write and fallback append.

1-4.label: Performance evidence lanes under ownership migration

decisions.answer: Performance is a validation dimension under ownership migration, not an independent steering tree.
decisions.note: Each slice records trend evidence; bounded performance exploit opens only when it supports ownership progress or user usability.

1-4.notes: Performance trend evidence belongs under ownership slices; do not let performance become an independent steering tree.

1-5.label: Agent Sufficiency and graph semantics guardrails
1-5.notes: Guardrails apply when graph semantics, Explore output, language coverage, or user-facing sufficiency claims change.

1-6.label: No-go defer and research archive

decisions.answer: Keep no-go, defer, and research routes as explicit roadmap subtrees.
decisions.note: Prevents future agents from re-entering already tested failure modes.

1-6.notes: Archive no-go/defer/research branches directly in the roadmap so future agents do not repeat prior dead ends.

decisions.answer: Build the map only; do not split implementation issues in this stage.
decisions.note: The point of this stage is to return to the start and rebuild navigation from accumulated facts.

1-3-1.label: Facts protocol first slice for LowerName QualifiedName FileNodes

decisions.answer: Start at the facts input layer by making Rust-produced facts a stable protocol boundary.
decisions.note: Do not start by changing final reference disambiguation semantics.

decisions.answer: Cover LowerName, QualifiedName, and FileNodes with explicit keep, no-go, or diagnostic-only status.
decisions.note: Use prior evidence instead of redefining the full resolver input surface in one step.

decisions.answer: Expose factsProtocol diagnostics for LowerName, QualifiedName, and FileNodes in rust-hybrid profile artifacts.
decisions.note: No resolver semantics or graph output changed; this is a protocol-status diagnostic slice.

1-3-1.notes: Completed first narrow slice: profile artifacts now expose factsProtocol shape status for LowerName, QualifiedName, and FileNodes. This establishes candidate-set-only protocol ownership diagnostics without changing final reference disambiguation semantics or graph output.

1-3-2.label: Reference disambiguation semantic migration slices

decisions.answer: Use shadow/double-read semantic replay before moving any reference disambiguation decision to the main path.
decisions.note: Rust/protocol may produce replay decisions for selected references, but TypeScript remains final owner of graph output in this slice.

decisions.answer: Start with direct ESM named import/export binding replay.
decisions.note: Cover import { foo } from repo-local relative or path-alias targets to exported foo; exclude default, namespace, type-only, barrel chains, package resolution, and fuzzy/name-matching ranking.

decisions.answer: Record semantic replay evidence in profile artifact diagnostics.
decisions.note: Use a semanticReplay diagnostic bucket; do not write SQLite debug tables and do not create durable benchmark artifacts for every process run.

decisions.answer: Use a medium taxonomy for direct named import/export replay.
decisions.note: Include import-target-unresolved, export-symbol-missing, multiple-export-candidates, ts-unresolved-rust-resolved, ts-resolved-rust-unresolved, different-target-node, and different-resolution-method. Keep unsupported syntax families out of this slice.

decisions.answer: Track implementation in #521.
decisions.note: Issue covers semanticReplay profile diagnostics for direct named ESM import/export shadow replay.

1-3-2.notes: Completed by #521. Implemented semanticReplay profile diagnostics for direct named ESM import shadow replay, including equivalent replay counts and fallback taxonomy for unresolved export symbols. TypeScript remains final graph-output owner; replay does not write SQLite state.

1-3-3.label: Finalization cleanup and edge write ownership slices

decisions.answer: Guarded edge-write ownership slice
decisions.note: Prefer moving validated resolver/protocol decisions toward guarded edge-write ownership before cleanup ownership. Keep the slice narrow: no broad resolver semantic expansion, no package/default/namespace/re-export scope expansion by default.

decisions.answer: Direct named import file/symbol edge write
decisions.note: Reuse the semanticReplay evidence area from #521. Start from direct named value imports with unique repo-local targets; defer LowerName and FileNodes/module-resolution edge-write routing to later slices.

decisions.answer: Only imported symbol usage edges
decisions.note: This slice should prove one per-reference semantic edge path for direct named imports. Do not include file-level binding dependency edges in this slice; keep those for module/file dependency ownership work.

decisions.answer: Direct main-path write with fail-closed guards
decisions.note: Do not add another shadow-only middle state. Write only when direct named value import usage has a unique repo-local target and passes endpoint/duplicate guards; all unsupported or ambiguous cases skip with taxonomy.

decisions.answer: Allow guarded additive rust-finalization usage edges with target parity
decisions.note: Do not replace existing TypeScript-owned edges in this slice. Graph output may gain rust-finalization usage edges when target parity is preserved or when the edge was previously missing; duplicate-safe behavior is required.

decisions.answer: Use medium-grained taxonomy
decisions.note: Track unsupported-import-shape, type-only-import, import-target-unresolved, export-symbol-missing, multiple-export-candidates, usage-ref-missing, endpoint-invalid, duplicate-equivalent-edge, and non-repo-local-target. Avoid ultra-fine moduleResolution taxonomy in this slice.

decisions.answer: Add finalize.referenceResolutionBreakdown.guardedEdgeWrite
decisions.note: Keep guardedEdgeWrite beside semanticReplay. Include eligibleRefs, attemptedRefs, writtenEdges, skippedRefs, skipReasons, skipSamples, and edgeKindCounts so replay and guarded-write migration evidence are readable together.

decisions.answer: Use deterministic CLI/profile and graph parity tests only
decisions.note: Cover written direct named value import usage edges, skipped unsupported forms, duplicate-safe behavior, guardedEdgeWrite profile fields, and targeted rust-hybrid CLI tests. Do not run Agent Sufficiency A/B or real-repo smoke for this narrow slice.

decisions.answer: Write a narrow plan and publish 2-3 implementation issues
decisions.note: The plan should preserve the grilled boundaries. Issues should cover guarded direct named import usage edge write/profile diagnostics, skip taxonomy and duplicate-safe parity coverage, and closeout roadmap/decision evidence if needed.

decisions.answer: Do not mark 1-3-3 completed after this slice; create a child sub-node
decisions.note: This slice only covers guarded direct named import usage edge-write. Finalization cleanup and broader edge-write ownership remain under 1-3-3 for later slices.

1-3-3.notes: Third slice starts with a narrow guarded edge-write ownership slice. Cleanup remains a follow-up closeout concern unless this slice exposes a direct blocker.
